title: Brautag / Brew Day 2025/26 (Non-BC Holiday Post)
summary: This is a non-Business Central post about a traditional Bavarian home brewing day, documenting the step-by-step process of brewing a Märzen beer including mashing, sparging, boiling, cooling, and fermentation with detailed explanations of brewing chemistry and techniques.
key_points: Multi-step mashing at different temperatures extracts different types of sugars to balance fermentability, body, and flavor in the final beer
Different hop varieties are used for different purposes: noble hops for aroma and traditional character, high-alpha hops for efficient bittering
A 90-minute boil sterilizes the wort, concentrates volume, extracts hop bitterness, removes off-flavors, and clarifies through protein coagulation
Post-boil cooling can be done rapidly or slowly overnight depending on equipment and water conservation priorities before yeast pitching
Fermentation takes 6-10 weeks, after which the finished beer is kegged with CO2 for carbonation and serving

quotes.text: By using multiple temperature steps, you control the balance between fermentable sugars (higher alcohol, drier finish) vs non-fermentable sugars (body, sweetness, mouthfeel).
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the core principle of mashing that determines the final beer's character and quality
